hook.line: Sometimes you do two things at once: drive and talk, study and work. Spanish has a small phrase that glues them together.
hook.es: Estudia y trabaja a la vez.
hook.en: She studies and works at the same time.

examples.es: Vale hace pan y a la vez atiende el teléfono.
examples.en: Vale makes bread and answers the phone at the same time.

examples.es: Es útil y a la vez bonito.
examples.en: It's useful and pretty at the same time.

examples.es: Mariana escribe y escucha música al mismo tiempo.
examples.en: Mariana writes and listens to music at the same time.

examples.es: Ella cocinaba; mientras tanto, yo lavaba los platos.
examples.en: She was cooking; meanwhile, I was washing the dishes.

examples.es: Tomás sirve el café; mientras tanto, Vale abre la caja.
examples.en: Tomás serves the coffee; meanwhile, Vale opens the till.

rule:
*A la vez* and *al mismo tiempo* both mean "at the same time". Use them when one person does two things: *Hernando maneja y habla a la vez.* They also join two qualities: *útil y a la vez bonito*.

When two different people do two things, use *mientras tanto* (meanwhile), in its own bit of the sentence, set off by commas.

The verbs do not change, and neither do these phrases.
smallPrint: Teachers call this simultaneity: two actions or qualities happening or holding together.

readAndPick.es: Vale hace pan y a la vez atiende el teléfono.
options: Vale makes bread and then answers the phone.
Vale makes bread so she can answer the phone.
Vale makes bread and answers the phone at the same time.

readAndPick.es: Es útil y a la vez bonito.
options: It's useful and pretty at the same time.
It's useful but not pretty.
It's useful because it's pretty.

readAndPick.es: Tomás sirve el café; mientras tanto, Vale abre la caja.
options: Tomás serves coffee after Vale opens the till.
Tomás serves coffee; meanwhile, Vale opens the till.
Tomás serves coffee while he opens the till.
Everyone spoke in turn.
Everyone spoke once.
Everyone spoke at once.

readAndPick.es: Mariana escribe y escucha música al mismo tiempo.
options: Mariana writes after she listens to music.
Mariana writes about music.
Mariana writes and listens to music at the same time.

readAndPick.es: Ella cocinaba; mientras tanto, yo lavaba los platos.
options: She cooked and then I washed the dishes.
She was cooking; meanwhile, I was washing the dishes.
She was cooking while she washed the dishes.

readAndPick.es: No puedo hablar y escribir a la vez.
options: I can't talk and write at the same time.
I can't talk or write later.
I can't talk about writing.

readAndPick.es: Es un lugar viejo y a la vez moderno.
options: It's a place that was old and is now modern.
It's an old place, but not a modern one.
It's an old place and, at the same time, a modern one.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hernando maneja y habla ___.* (*a la vez* or *mientras tanto*) Hernando drives and talks at the same time.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando maneja y habla a la vez.
accept: Hernando maneja y habla al mismo tiempo.
yourTurn.why: One person does two things, so *a la vez*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Tomás sirve el café; ___, Vale abre la caja.* (*a la vez* or *mientras tanto*) Tomás serves the coffee; meanwhile, Vale opens the till.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás sirve el café; mientras tanto, Vale abre la caja.
accept: Tomás sirve el café. Mientras tanto, Vale abre la caja.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It's useful and pretty at the same time.
yourTurn.answer: Es útil y a la vez bonito.
accept: Es útil y bonito a la vez.
Es útil y al mismo tiempo bonito.
yourTurn.why: *A la vez* sits between the two qualities.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I can't talk and write at the same time.
yourTurn.answer: No puedo hablar y escribir a la vez.
accept: No puedo hablar y escribir al mismo tiempo.
yourTurn.why: One person, two actions: *a la vez* at the end.
*A la vez* works for a whole group too.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it with *al mismo tiempo*: *Mariana escribe y escucha música a la vez.*
yourTurn.answer: Mariana escribe y escucha música al mismo tiempo.
yourTurn.why: The two phrases mean the same, and *al* is *a* plus *el*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, with *mientras tanto*: She was cooking; meanwhile, I was washing the dishes.
yourTurn.answer: Ella cocinaba; mientras tanto, yo lavaba los platos.
accept: Ella cocinaba. Mientras tanto, yo lavaba los platos.

pitfalls.wrong: Vale hace pan y mientras tanto atiende el teléfono.
pitfalls.right: Vale hace pan y a la vez atiende el teléfono.
pitfalls.why: *Mientras tanto* needs two separate people; for one person's two actions use *a la vez*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hablo y escribo en el mismo tiempo.
pitfalls.right: Hablo y escribo al mismo tiempo.
pitfalls.why: English says "at the same time", but Spanish says *al mismo tiempo*, with *a* and *el* joined.

pitfalls.wrong: Ella cocinaba, a la vez yo lavaba los platos.
pitfalls.right: Ella cocinaba; mientras tanto, yo lavaba los platos.

personal: What two things do you do at once every day? Say it with *a la vez*, for example: *Yo… y… a la vez.*
